claims.short_label: February 1865 Union veteran-to-Yale transmission and late 1872 Twain vehicular extension
claims.statement: Returning Union student-veterans introduced awareness of 'shebang' into the Yale Literary Magazine by February 1865 (initially mocking regional Indianapolis usage six years before naturalized campus slang in Bagg 1871), while wheeled-vehicle usage ('THE CHARTERED SHEBANG' in Twain's 1872 Roughing It) arose nearly two decades after the tavern/hut sense.
claims.rationale: In the February 1865 Yale Literary Magazine (CERT-2000-211), returning 100-day student-soldiers quote 'what owns this shebang' explicitly as mocked Indianapolis ('Injunoppolis') regional speech prior to full Yale campus naturalization in Bagg (1871, CERT-2000-222), partially supporting soldier-mediated campus transmission while refuting antebellum Yale origin lore and proving Twain's 1872 vehicle usage (CERT-2000-223) was secondary.

evidence_boundary.establishes: February 1865 student-veteran awareness of 'shebang' in the Yale Literary Magazine (quoted as Midwestern speech), naturalized Yale campus slang by 1871, and post-bellum emergence of the 1872 vehicle sense.
evidence_boundary.does_not_establish: Full campus naturalization of 'shebang' at Yale as early as February 1865 or any antebellum college/carriage currency.
evidence_boundary.remaining_uncertainty: Exact campus transition at Yale between mocking Midwestern 'shebang' in February 1865 and routine student room-slang in Bagg (1871).

limitations: CERT-2000-211 and misdate audit record CERT-2000-121 cite the exact same February 1865 passage (1 witness).

claims.case_section: 5. Origin Pathways and Rejected Archival Leads
claims.short_label: Anglo-Irish 'shebeen' + expressive 'che-bang!' remodeling vs. weakened 'char-à-bancs' and refuted contact myths
claims.statement: Remodeling of immigrant Anglo-Irish 'shebeen' (< Irish 'séibín'/'síbín', oxytonic illicit alehouse) onto American expressive 'che-bang!' / '-bang' (1849–1858) is consistent with 1854 tavern semantics and oxytonic stress, whereas French 'char-à-bancs' lacks tavern/hut semantics before 1872 and 'cabane', 'Scheveningen', 'Schuppen', and 'chabola' are refuted.
claims.rationale: Per Commit 5db37e1, co-temporal Northeastern 'shebeen' and 'che-bang!' witnesses (CERT-2000-301..305, 101, 104, 114..117) align with early saloon usage without proving the unwritten oral blend, while 'char-à-bancs' (306, 307) was a genteel European carriage and Confederate 'cabane' (308), Dutch (312), German (313), and post-1852 Basque-Spanish 'chabola' (314) fail chronologically and phonologically.

evidence_boundary.establishes: Co-temporal pre-1860 American currency of 'shebeen' and 'che-bang!', carriage restriction of 1830s 'char-à-bancs', and exclusion of four folk contact etymons.
evidence_boundary.does_not_establish: Direct documentary proof of the oral 'shebeen' x 'che-bang!' blending event.
evidence_boundary.remaining_uncertainty: Whether 'char-à-bancs' secondarily reinforced '<ch->' spelling or Twain's 1872 cart joke.

limitations: Qualified per Commit 5db37e1: consistent with tavern/stress evidence without claiming proof of ultimate coinage.
resolution_criteria: Locate an 1845–1855 American text explicitly treating 'shebeen' and 'chebang'/'shebang' as variants.
